title: Clap against a data center, go to jail.
body: 404 Media reports that a high school physics teacher in Emporia, Kansas got arrested last week for clapping. Lux Claridge, 37, showed up with family to oppose a hyperscale data center planned for 1,000 acres of rural land. Commissioners had warned the room against clapping, snapping, or rude comments. Claridge kept clapping for the speakers who were against it, so police pulled them out and booked them for interference with law enforcement.

Claridge is not alone. 404 Media has watched the same scene play out around the country, a man in Claremore, Oklahoma cuffed for speaking too long, protesters arrested at a meeting in Port Washington. When 404 asked Emporia for the arrest report, police refused, saying releasing it could "interfere with ongoing investigative efforts." For a clapping charge. Claridge, out on bail, called the whole thing "an inconvenience" and said it wasn't stopping them from speaking out, "or I guess, clapping."

Data centers are the new gold rush, and local governments are already treating the people who live next to them as a problem to manage. Public comment is supposed to be where residents get heard. Turns out it runs smoother when they stay quiet.
